questions.q: When a validation rule's Error Condition Formula evaluates to TRUE, what happens?
options: The record saves and a warning is logged for later review
The field is automatically cleared and the save proceeds
The save is blocked and the configured Error Message is shown
Nothing — TRUE means the rule passed and the record is valid
questions.explain: A validation rule formula is effectively a trap: TRUE means the bad condition was found, so Salesforce blocks the save and shows the Error Message.

questions.q: Why does the phone-format rule include NOT(ISBLANK(Phone)) alongside the REGEX check?
options: Without it, a blank Phone field would also fail the REGEX test, making the field effectively required
REGEX cannot run unless ISBLANK is evaluated first
It makes the rule run faster
ISBLANK is required syntax for every validation rule, regardless of content
questions.explain: REGEX against an empty string fails the pattern match, so without the ISBLANK guard, leaving Phone blank would incorrectly trigger the rule.

questions.q: Which data quality dimension do duplicate rules and matching rules primarily address?
options: Accuracy
Consistency
Completeness
Uniqueness
questions.explain: Duplicate and matching rules exist to catch the same real-world thing being recorded twice — that's uniqueness, distinct from accuracy, consistency, or completeness.

questions.q: What does PRIORVALUE(field) return in a validation rule?
options: The default value defined on the field
The value the field had before the current edit, on an update
The most common value for that field across the org
A random sample value used for testing the rule
questions.explain: PRIORVALUE compares against the field's previous value, which is useful for rules that should only fire when a specific field changes.

questions.q: Why can an overly strict validation rule actually hurt data quality?
options: Strict rules always slow down page load times significantly
Overly strict rules automatically disable all other validation rules on the object
Users route around a rule with no reasonable exception by entering junk just to pass it
Strict rules cannot be combined with AND or OR
questions.explain: When a rule blocks a legitimate edge case with no way through, users often type placeholder junk just to satisfy it — worse for data quality than no rule.
